target_customer: Men (and their partners) who want to test, improve or freeze sperm without visiting a clinic, including cancer patients, TRT users and people in high-risk jobs
problem: Male fertility testing and sperm freezing required awkward, expensive clinic visits and there was no trusted, convenient option; the founder started after a friend facing cancer treatment found no trustworthy storage.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer mail-in testing kits plus annual storage subscriptions, plus B2B partnerships and insurance
product_category: Male fertility testing and sperm freezing (digital health)

founders.name: Khaled Kteily
education: Master in public policy, Harvard Kennedy School

founders.name: Sarah Steinle
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page without a bio.

competitors.name: Dadi
competitors.what: Mail-in sperm testing and storage startup
competitors.funding_then: $2M raise reported January 2019 (per a TechCrunch piece linked from the 2020 article; the linked piece was not opened)

technical_complexity.rationale: Logistics, lab partnerships (analysis by Andrology Labs, storage by third-party cryo providers) and a consumer web flow; no novel technology, with clinical-quality operations and compliance as the harder parts.

defensibility.rationale: Stored samples create a recurring relationship, but kits and storage are outsourced and a similar competitor (Dadi) already existed; the edge was brand and trust positioning.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dadi, the closest rival, was acquired by Ro in March 2022 (per search summary), showing consumer-health platforms were consolidating the category; no source shows a major player copying Legacy before its 2022 Series B.

market_need_then: Legacy said about four million couples face fertility challenges and almost half of kit purchases came from female partners; clinic options were described as awkward and expensive, and the 2018 TechCrunch story cited a friend's cancer treatment as the trigger.

branding.domain_note: Operates on givelegacy.com (prefix variant, not the exact .com); acquisition history not found.

identity.visual_style: Clean consumer-health design with quiz call-to-action
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, direct and slightly playful ('we're not judging'); 'Your sperm is your future'

branding.brand_signature: 'Swiss bank' positioning: calls itself the Swiss private bank for men's most valuable assets, with client IDs and privacy emphasized
branding.community_and_virality: Site lists press logos (New York Magazine, Fast Company) and a 4.9 rating from 130+ Google reviews; the 2023 head-of-marketing hire aimed at making Legacy a household name per a search summary.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct privacy and Swiss-bank positioning and consistent tone, with notable press, but no independent evidence that the brand itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Legacy raised about $45M by May 2022 and says it grew revenue roughly sevenfold in 2020 and fourfold in 2021; in July 2024 it raised $7.5M and said it would reach profitability. It moved from a high-priced 2018 offer ($1,000 to $10,000 packages) to a mail-in kit at about $195 and added insurance and B2B channels. Growth figures are company claims and the later small round suggests slower funding, so it is a surviving but not clearly breakout company.
notes: Directory/YC say founded 2019 but TechCrunch covered Legacy in November 2018 and InsideHook says 2018, so 2018 is used. The 2018 round date is not exact and predates the S19 batch. The 2019 seed and 2024 round dates and details come from press-release listings and a search summary, not full reads. Total raised is reported inconsistently (about $15M in 2021, $45M in 2022, 'almost $50M' on YC). Dadi's Jan 2019 raise and Ro acquisition (March 2022) come from search summaries. 2018-era pricing was Bronze $1,000 and Platinum $10,000 per TechCrunch. Web Archive skipped.
